scope: Local layout review; no application implementation or deployment

steps.finding: The header is stable and the palette is clear. The bottom bar begins after the sidebar, so Play sits at x=335 rather than the x=31 used in Composer.
steps.recommendation: Use a full-width bottom bar outside the work area. Keep instrument choices and performer details in the left panel.

steps.finding: The normal header remains, but the instrument area is tall. The score receives much less height than the palette and staff can extend beyond its visible area.
steps.recommendation: Shorten the palette heading and combine selection information into a compact strip; give the score the recovered space.

steps.finding: The workspace tabs, title, Files and More disappear. Visual style, camera and playback replace them. Play moves to the top right.
steps.recommendation: Retain the regular header and bottom bar. Keep the sphere and compact read-only score in the center.

steps.finding: The ordinary header and full-width bottom playback bar remain. The current song is Untitled while library rows offer other songs through Open.
steps.recommendation: Keep the structure and explicitly identify the current song in the playback area. Browsing and filtering should preserve playback; opening another song should load it paused.

steps.finding: The first passage contains bass notes but they are initially below the visible portion of the score. The top instrument panel takes about 193 pixels at this viewport.
steps.recommendation: Reduce the instrument panel height and retain section/passage navigation beside the score. Consider opening the score at the relevant register as a separate usability refinement.

steps.finding: The dialog combines duplicate file actions, title, Theme, Meter, score operations and loop-range settings. Its lower controls require scrolling.
steps.recommendation: Keep saving/loading in Files; group appearance together; keep Meter and score length in Song settings. Put loop-range access beside Loop and note operations near the selection.

steps.finding: Files provides saving, loading, import, export and recovery with explanatory copy. The same core actions are also present in More.
steps.recommendation: Make Files the consistent home for these actions. Retain the useful explanation and recovery behavior.

steps.finding: The regular header and bottom transport remain while help scrolls in the center.
steps.recommendation: Keep this structure, showing which current song the persistent playback controls operate on.

steps.finding: Pitch, duration, performer, note volume and actions appear as an extra row, reducing the score viewport. The volume label clearly distinguishes note volume from master volume.
steps.recommendation: Give selection tools a predictable location and keep master controls in the fixed bottom bar. Choose between a reserved compact row and a side inspector only after comparing available score space.

steps.health: Useful tools; details can be buried
steps.finding: The selected performer appears below the complete instrument palette. Its location and move actions lie below the visible sidebar area at this viewport. Play is at (335,650).
steps.recommendation: Scroll the palette independently or provide a compact expandable selected-performer area so the current selection remains easy to reach.

steps.health: Keep the presentation; replace the surrounding controls
steps.finding: The sphere, instruments, Mario and compact score work together well. The top bar is still entirely different and omits BPM and master volume. Play is at approximately (801,30).
steps.recommendation: Use the same header, title and bottom transport as the other workspaces. Place Visual style, Reset view and Slow rotate in a consistent corner of the sphere in Placement and Performance.

proposal.Header: Same brand, workspace tabs, song title, Files and settings access in every workspace. Keep their order and positions stable. Performance stays an ordinary selected tab; remove the separate Exit Performance requirement.
proposal.Playback bar: Always full width at the bottom, below every sidebar. Stable left-to-right order: Play/Pause, Stop, Loop, position; then BPM and master volume. Keep Play’s size fixed when its label becomes Pause. Show the current song when browsing Library or FAQ.
proposal.Work area: Placement: instruments left, sphere right. Composer: compact instrument strip above the large score, with editing tools beside the score. Performance: large sphere and compact score. Library and FAQ: scrolling content. Shared controls stay outside the scrolling area.
proposal.Sphere controls: Visual style, Reset view and Slow rotate in the same sphere corner in Placement and Performance. These do not replace navigation. Appearance changes remain separate from sound-set changes.
proposal.Song and selection settings: Files owns save/load/import/export/recovery. Song settings owns meter and score length. Loop-range access sits beside Loop. Note and performer properties stay contextual. Undo/Redo need one stable location and disabled states rather than shifting other controls.
proposal.Playback behavior: Switching workspaces and browsing the library preserve play/pause, position, tempo, volume and loop. Opening another composition is explicit and loads paused. A musical edit retains the current pause-to-edit behavior. Loop remains one toggle and Stop remains stop-and-rewind.

decisions.Play location: Recommend the fixed lower-left bottom bar. Placing Play left of the treble clef is a coherent alternative only if that same control position is reserved in Placement and Library, which have no visible staff. Do not add a second Play control.
decisions.Performance score height: The persistent bottom bar takes some height. Keep the score above it and let the sphere use the remaining space; compare dense scores before shrinking the notation. An adjustable score divider is a possible later refinement, not a prerequisite.
decisions.Selection tools: A compact reserved row avoids vertical movement when selecting a note, but costs height even when nothing is selected. A side inspector keeps score height, but costs width. Start with a shorter palette and compare before introducing a sidebar.
decisions.Meaning of Track: The current top tabs are Placement, Composer, Performance, Library and FAQ. Track has not been identified as a current screen. Pending clarification, song-wide settings are treated as Song settings, while performer-specific controls remain contextual.
decisions.Narrow screens: Use one consistent compact header and bottom-control arrangement at a given screen size. Overflow lower-priority settings before allowing Play/Stop/Loop to move or vanish. This run inspected the default desktop viewport; narrow-screen acceptance remains unverified.
